N01.statement: When a member starts a mark (R01), the room calls others to place (P01); after a call, the room builds the mark and members report it (P03); once the mark stands, the room keeps it (P05).
N01.level: element: a chain of three arrows, each with its own mechanism
N01.rival: The order is how threads are made: a call is a thread's title and the build reports are comments under it, so the order follows the coders' choice of turns.
N01.decides: The null holds each room's coded turns and hours fixed. With the joining lines stripped out, the call still comes before the build in 78 of 126 rooms (A01), and in 50 rooms a build report replies to a call in the same thread (121 transitions).
N01.falsify_elsewhere: On another shared surface with a per-account rate limit, groups would build before anyone calls as often as after, or keep a finished work no more often than an unfinished one.
N01.boundary: Where a member places alone before any call, the call follows the first build (A01's bound); where the mark was found already placed or a rival attacked first, upkeep comes first (A03's bound).

N02.statement: When a room keeps a mark (P05), it turns to other rooms: it talks borders with neighbours (P08), asks other rooms for help (P16) and joins coalitions under attack (P17). Where border talk comes before upkeep, it mostly offers terms before any damage.
N02.level: dimension: Maintenance to Order without law; the three arrows share the mechanism that keeping a work brings a room into relations with other rooms; A19 is thin
N02.rival: Neighbours were there from the room's first post, so the talk comes with the spot and not from keeping it.
N02.decides: On the late side only 6 of 15 rooms hold A04's order. In the 166 rooms where border talk comes first, two coders read the first border talk in 40: it offers terms before any damage in 19 of 26 to 36 of 38 of the records that bear on it (Cohen's kappa 0.19; A04's bound).
N02.falsify_elsewhere: On another shared surface, groups that keep their work would meet their neighbours no more often after upkeep than before it.
N02.boundary: Late rooms that arrive at a full surface or enter through another room's offer (A04's, A19's bounds); hosts ruling on guests (P19, a candidate).

N03.statement: A call to place can turn members against a rival's work (P01 to P09). The same room answers the call to attack: members refuse it, in written replies usually with a reason (F-014), the room reins in the attackers or apologises (P07), or points to a truce (P08). Where the attack goes on, the rooms carry the contest on in talk (P18).
N03.level: element: a chain; A16 and A17 share the mechanism that a contest is answered by the order between rooms (Contention to Order without law); A15 and A18 have their own
N03.rival: Restraint is coded only when there is an attack call to refuse, so the order is built into the coding (A16 is partly constitutive).
N03.decides: Sparing comes first, with no call, in 22 of 104 rooms. In 52 rooms a refusal by another member replies to a specific attack call within minutes (127 transitions). In written, coded replies, refusals give a reason in 23 of 38 read pairs and acceptances in 2 of 14 (F-014), a ratio of kinds set by the draw; on calls to place, refusals gave a reason in 3 of 3 and acceptances in 6 of 31 (F-023). The coding of themes does not produce this. More than half of all calls carry no written reply, so the asymmetry is about what members wrote.
N03.falsify_elsewhere: In another population, attack calls would draw no refusal inside the calling group, or refusals would come as bare as acceptances.
N03.boundary: Colour factions whose faith names the rival (thebluecorner): the model tells their attack calls, not why their faith picks the rival.

N04.statement: After members report a mark done (P03), the room celebrates it (P11), records what it celebrated (P12) and carries the record on (P13). Placement stops at hour 73 for every room; after it, rooms can celebrate, record, curate the record and carry it on, and no one can place.
N04.level: dimension: Coordination without command to Imprinting (A07), then inside Imprinting (A08, A09)
N04.rival: Celebrations and records cluster at the end of the event in every room, so the order is the clock's and not the room's.
N04.decides: The null shuffles labels within each room's own hours, so a shared clock cannot produce the order. A07 holds on the early side in 38 of 65 rooms; A08 holds on the late side in only 8 of 15.
N04.falsify_elsewhere: In another episode with an imposed end, groups would record before they celebrate as often as after.
N04.boundary: Where the clock cut the work unfinished, members mark the attempt (A07's bound); late rooms often record first (A08's bound).

N05.statement: When a room calls for hands in a standing sub (P01), the host sub's moderators and members draw a line around canvas talk (P20): a megathread, removals by rule, a canvas sub, objections to the flood.
N05.level: dimension: Critical mass to Host framing
N05.rival: A removal needs a post to remove, so the line follows a call by definition (A20 is partly constitutive).
N05.decides: 23 rooms draw the line first. Counted by actor while the canvas runs, the calls come before the host sub's rulings in 102 of 118 rooms and before members' objections in 57 of 64.
N05.falsify_elsewhere: In another passing event inside standing communities, the communities would contain it as often before any member posts about it as after.
N05.boundary: Subs opened for the canvas, which have no prior business to protect; the record does not show how many there are (78 of 705 rooms have no posts in the week before, and when they began is not shown).

N06.statement: When the room's upkeep needs more placements than its members can make (P05), members turn to scripts and spare accounts (P14).
N06.level: dimension: Maintenance to Coordination without command
N06.rival: The members who run scripts are the members who keep the work, so the order follows who is active, not strain.
N06.decides: The reverse order, scripts before upkeep, holds in 41 of 203 rooms, below its null mean (F-005); in 117 transitions in 53 rooms a script or spare account answers upkeep within minutes.
N06.falsify_elsewhere: Under a per-account rate limit elsewhere, groups would turn to automation before any upkeep as often as after.
N06.boundary: Rooms that scripted the building from the start, and spare accounts used for an attack before any upkeep (A06's bound).

N07.statement: Rooms align their members' placing without deciding how they are organized: members answer a call in a bare line (P15), a design argued in a thread is settled by a posted template (P04), and a decided element of order appears in 46 of 705 rooms (C01). In 233 of the 370 rooms that called for hands, the record reports a work up after the first call (F-021); the others tried.
N07.level: element: two theorised arrows and claims on findings (F-021, F-023, F-006)
N07.rival: Members decided their organization in chats that the record does not hold, so the absence of decided order is the instrument's.
N07.decides: The record counts its parts: a work reported up after the first call in 233 of 370 rooms with calls (F-021); written acceptances bare in 25 of 31 replies to calls to place (F-023); decided order in 46 of 705 rooms (F-006). The rival is not decided: chats reached the thread with a decision in 33 rooms, and the claim that decided order is absent elsewhere is about rooms writing in public, and weak (contract section 5).
N07.falsify_elsewhere: In another population whose chats are on the record, decisions about who does what would appear wherever the work was large.
N07.boundary: Rooms that govern a territory for a colour or vet others' requests to build, where decided order is coded more often, the gap lying in the smaller rooms (F-006's bound). Rooms whose record reports no work up after their calls, where the room tried (137 of 370; F-021).

N08.statement: When a room judges it has too few hands to hold its spot (K02), it stops fighting for it and moves (P10), and members keep calling for the new spot.
N08.level: dimension: Critical mass to Order without law; one thin arrow
N08.rival: Rooms move by a coalition's plan or by choice, and the judgment of too few hands is written after the move.
N08.decides: The order holds in 11 of 21 rooms. Read whole at C5c-09, the judgment came before a move after a loss in 10 of the 20 rooms that moved (9 if a coalition's move is read so), voiced for the room in 7; in the other 10 the loss itself prompted the move (F-019). A late room wrote its judgment after the move (guatemala, h79.1).
N08.falsify_elsewhere: Elsewhere, groups that lose ground would move as often with no voiced doubt as with it.
N08.boundary: Rooms inside a coalition that move by the coalition's plan (A10's bound). Rooms that judge their hands too few after a loss and give the work up instead: of 36 rooms that voiced such doubt and lost their work, 10 moved and 11 gave the work up (F-019).

N09.statement: A settled border (P08) opens a channel through which the two rooms trade help (P16). Sparing a neighbour's work (P07) follows border talk in more rooms than chance gives, but the line a settled border would give is theorised: the first sparing names a border or deal in 17 of 124 rooms, and mostly states the room's own norm (F-020).
N09.level: inside Order without law; two thin arrows, A05's mechanism theorised
N09.rival: Sparing is tacit and comes first, and help comes with the neighbour, not with the border.
N09.decides: Read whole at C5c-09: the first help names a deal, border, truce, alliance, an exchange or the neighbour relation in 63 of 127 rooms where border talk comes first, against 23 of 67 where help comes first (F-020). Both arrows beat their nulls' 95th percentile by a little: A05 by 0.013, A14 by 0.009.
N09.falsify_elsewhere: Elsewhere, neighbours who settle a border would spare and help each other no more often than neighbours who never talked.
N09.boundary: Neighbours who spare each other with no talk at all, on the room's own norm (Live and let live; F-020).
